summary: You have a clear case for reef monitoring, with footnoted sources and well-identified users in marine and conservation science. The main gaps are technical. The geostationary orbit at 600 km cannot hold the reef in view, so the design needs rethinking before progress can be judged. Your progress evidence is also thin: you have completed tutorials but no results yet. Addressing these points would strengthen the report considerably.
next_steps: Revisit your orbit choice. A geostationary orbit sits about 35,786 km above the equator, so a 600 km orbit cannot keep the reef in view. Select an orbit suited to near-real-time reef imaging, and include a brief trade-off between altitude, revisit time and resolution.

Make the schedule consistent: place editing in weeks 7 and 8 in both the text and the Gantt chart. Add contingencies for delays or STK problems, and correct the acidification and bathymetry claims so each statement matches its source.

Produce first STK results, such as orbit parameters, coverage or revisit calculations, with a short interpretation. Then add software and information-sources sections, with a reference list that matches your in-text citations.

criteria.C1: Your rationale is clear: reef monitoring is well motivated, you identify marine and conservation scientists as users, and you explain why reefs matter to people. To reach the Accomplished band, define quantitative objectives and requirements (resolution, revisit, coverage) and develop other users such as reef managers and tourism operators. Correct your orbit, bleaching and bathymetry claims, and turn your footnote URLs into a proper reference list.
criteria.C2: You have a feasible plan: the Gantt chart shows stages, status colours and deadlines. However, the text places editing in weeks 7 and 8 while the chart shows weeks 9 and 10, so these must be reconciled. To reach the Accomplished band, add explicit contingencies and variation provisions, tie the schedule to the mission narrative, and list your information sources with references.
criteria.C3: Your progress so far is mainly reading, background research and STK tutorials 1 to 4. No preliminary calculations, orbit parameters or STK outputs are presented, and your only design decision (GEO at 600 km) is technically incorrect. To reach at least the Adequate band, show initial results such as orbit calculations or coverage plots, with a short interpretation explaining what they mean for your mission.
criteria.C4: Your sections are clearly headed and the report reads reasonably well, with footnotes matched to superscripts. To improve, give the Gantt chart a numbered caption and define its colour coding. Remove informal phrasing such as 'maybe only one is required' and 'More STK simulations needed'. Add the software and information-sources sections the brief asks for, and convert footnotes into a consistent reference list.
